quarterly_data.signal: First-half results by product (results presentation for March - August 2026): semiconductor-related equipment sales JPY 67,138 million (122.8% of the prior-year half; a record, per the deck), analysis equipment JPY 1,304 million (90.6%), FPD-related equipment JPY 3,936 million (120.8%), life-science equipment JPY 376 million (102.8%), parts / repair and other JPY 6,977 million (118.5%); average rate JPY 158 per USD (JPY 149 a year earlier). Quarterly sales rose 14% from the previous quarter, a record for the second consecutive quarter, led by semiconductor-related equipment, up 22% quarter on quarter to JPY 36,898 million in Q2 (June - August 2026); Q2 operating profit rose 26% quarter on quarter to JPY 12,866 million. The company says analysis-equipment sales fell because customers' equipment acceptance slipped and parts procurement and production lead times lengthened.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 semiconductor-related equipment sales JPY 67,138 million (122.8%); Q2 semiconductor-related equipment sales JPY 36,898 million (+22% QoQ); Q2 operating profit JPY 12,866 million (+26% QoQ)

quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor-related equipment orders (results presentation): Q2 (June - August 2026) orders received JPY 78,509 million, up 87% from the previous quarter, 3.2 times the prior-year quarter and a record for the third consecutive quarter; order backlog a record JPY 103,863 million, up 67% quarter on quarter and 2.3 times a year earlier. The company attributes the jump to a surge in sorter and stocker orders from a North American memory maker and higher EFEM orders for Chinese equipment makers. Analysis equipment: Q2 orders JPY 1,346 million, backlog JPY 5,604 million; FPD-related equipment: Q2 orders JPY 1,995 million, backlog JPY 1,127 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 semiconductor-related equipment orders JPY 78,509 million (+87% QoQ, 3.2 times YoY); backlog JPY 103,863 million (+67% QoQ, 2.3 times YoY)

quarterly_data.signal: First-half sales by region of the customer's headquarters (results presentation): US JPY 23,901 million (30%), China JPY 20,902 million (26%), Taiwan JPY 19,406 million (24%), Japan JPY 4,827 million (6%), Korea JPY 3,971 million (5%), Vietnam JPY 2,999 million (4%). The company says the top three regions make up about 80% of quarterly sales; the US hit a record, rising for a fourth straight quarter on sales to equipment makers and memory makers; China rose for a third straight quarter on sales to equipment makers; Taiwan fell from the previous quarter but stayed high, with foundry and memory-maker demand strong.
quarterly_data.figure: US JPY 23,901 million (30%); China JPY 20,902 million (26%); Taiwan JPY 19,406 million (24%)

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook stated in the results presentation: with the spread and wider use of generative AI, demand for high-performance, high-efficiency chips is growing and investment in semiconductor manufacturing equipment is accelerating; on HBM demand, investment in advanced memory and advanced logic is rising and device makers are expanding new capex and capacity; the company expects orders for its transfer equipment for advanced semiconductors and advanced packaging to keep rising. Revised full-year forecast by product: semiconductor-related equipment JPY 152,970 million (initial forecast JPY 132,480 million, 115.5%), analysis equipment JPY 3,490 million (initial JPY 4,225 million), FPD-related equipment JPY 7,349 million (initial JPY 10,090 million), life-science equipment JPY 1,616 million, parts / repair and other JPY 14,579 million, at JPY 158 per USD; the deck attributes the upward revision of full-year net sales to the surge in semiconductor-related equipment orders.
quarterly_data.figure: FY to February 2027 semiconductor-related equipment sales forecast JPY 152,970 million (initial JPY 132,480 million)

quarterly_data.signal: Procurement and supply (results presentation): the company sees a risk that elevated memory prices and longer lead times for procured parts raise procurement costs and delay securing needed materials, and says competition among companies to place orders early to secure materials is starting to overheat. In response to the surge in semiconductor-related equipment orders it is adding staff and securing production space at its Vietnamese and Chinese subsidiaries, and is placing advance orders, holding inventory and securing alternative parts and suppliers to limit the impact on delivery times.

Capacity expansion (results presentation): Vietnam - the start of operations at the new plant of RORZE ROBOTECH has been brought forward from Q1 2028 to Q4 2027 (first-phase construction to complete in Q4 2027); floor area after all new plants are complete versus the existing plant: assembly 60,000 m2 versus 14,400 m2 (5.2 times), parts manufacturing 53,200 m2 versus 18,150 m2 (3.9 times); the company is accelerating hiring at the Vietnam plant, raised wages in August, moved warehouse functions of the existing plant to an externally rented plant and is converting the freed space to clean rooms to enlarge the assembly floor. China (Shanghai Lingang) - the existing plant is moving to two-shift operation and a newly leased building nearby expands the plant, with operations scheduled to start from spring 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: Vietnam new plant start brought forward to Q4 2027 (from Q1 2028); assembly floor 60,000 m2 vs 14,400 m2 (5.2 times); Shanghai Lingang expansion from spring 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Other matters in the results presentation: the US patent suit brought by Kawasaki Heavy Industries against Rorze and its US subsidiary Rorze Automation (filed August 30, 2022; jury verdict March 13, 2026) was settled under a settlement agreement signed August 3, 2026; terms are confidential, the suit is finally resolved and the company says there is no impact on future business. Consolidated subsidiary Nanoverse: the customer is still evaluating the evaluation tool Nanoverse delivered, Nanoverse continues to work on issues raised by the customer, and the company is negotiating for an early completion of the evaluation so that sales can be booked within this fiscal year. Nanoverse's first-half impact on consolidated operating profit (JPY million): personnel 1,011, R&D 22, goodwill amortization 1,489, other SG&A 614.
quarterly_data.figure: settlement signed August 3, 2026; Nanoverse H1 goodwill amortization JPY 1,489 million
